community_of_christ.open_canon:
Community of Christ treats Scripture as the church's foundation and understands it as open to continuing witness. The Bible is the primary scripture. The Book of Mormon is accepted as an additional scripture and a witness to Jesus Christ, and the Doctrine and Covenants contains counsel received by the church over time.

The church holds that God continues to speak, and that new counsel is tested and accepted by the church in common, sometimes being added to the Doctrine and Covenants. An example is the counsel that led to the ordination of women. Members hold different views about how to understand the Book of Mormon, for example whether to read it as history, and the church does not press one reading. What they share is the conviction that revelation has not ended.
community_of_christ.temples:
Community of Christ has a Temple in Independence, Missouri, dedicated in 1994. It is understood as a place of worship, prayer, education and reconciliation, dedicated to the pursuit of peace, and it is generally open to visitors and to people of every faith or none.

This differs from the temples of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, where rites such as the endowment and sealings are performed and access is limited. Community of Christ does not practice those ordinances. The Temple's daily prayer for peace and its ministries of healing and study express the church's emphasis on peace, justice and the worth of all persons. It is one of the church's most visible signs of its own understanding of the Restoration tradition.
community_of_christ.degrees_of_glory:
The idea of degrees of glory, in which the afterlife has different kingdoms of glory, comes from a section of the Doctrine and Covenants that is part of the wider Latter Day Saint scriptures. In Community of Christ it is not a central teaching, and members do not emphasize a system of ranked rewards.

The church places its weight on the grace of God, the worth of all persons and the hope of resurrection through Jesus Christ. Questions about the details of the life to come are generally left to the mercy of God, with confidence that God wishes to bring people into wholeness. Members may hold varying personal views, and the church's emphasis falls on how to live faithfully in the present.
community_of_christ.mormon_label:
Members of Community of Christ generally do not call themselves Mormons. The church was known until 2001 as the Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints, or RLDS, and traces its history to those who did not follow Brigham Young to Utah but reorganized under the leadership of Joseph Smith III.

It understands itself as a Christian church within the Restoration tradition that began with Joseph Smith, but it is a separate body with its own name, its own governance and different practices. Many members are uncomfortable when others use the term Mormon for them, since in common speech it usually means the church headquartered in Salt Lake City. Members appreciate it when others call them by the church's present name, Community of Christ.
